2026-11-12.text:
Save your energy for tomorrow and the weekend! There’s a small chance of wind at Porteau and Squamish from a leftover southerly under the clouds, but it could fade quickly. Erwin could work until about 11am, but it’ll be gusty and light.

I’d call this a good day to rest. The rain also washed a lot of debris into the water, so if you do get out, watch for logs and fallen branches from the storm.

2026-11-11.text: The southeast gale is slow to reach the south shore, with Boundary Bay almost calm this morning, but the easterly is pumping off West Van: Point Atkinson read E 22 gusting 29 at 7am, ahead of the page. Erwin Park should be working  from first light (about 7:45am) to about 5:30pm, E 17 to 21 and gusty, so bring a small wing. No tide or weed worries there. Check before driving: Point Atkinson 20 or more from the east, go. East Beach in White Rock is the backup if the southeast fills in later; the FT and Boundary should be good for kiting but weeds may still be there for foiling.

2026-11-10.text: The Fraser easterly is on and Point Atkinson is running ahead of the page, E 21 at 6am and 19 gusting 24 at 7am, so Erwin Park should see about 15 to 17 against the page's 14. That's my pick, from first light (about 7:45am) until about 5:30pm, no tide limit, and Environment Canada calls southeast 20 to 30 this afternoon. Check before driving: Point Atkinson 18 or more from the east, go. I'm skipping Tsawwassen, where the last rider report had lots of weeds, and Boundary Bay, which likely has the same after these southeast storms. Jericho is the backup, buoy ENE 12 gusting 15.

2026-11-09.text:
Outflow is building. Pam Rocks read N 24 gusting 29 at 7am, up from 22 at 5am and a touch ahead of the page's 23. Pemberton is still 2 hPa above Vancouver, and Environment Canada's 4am update keeps the strong wind warning for Howe Sound, outflow 20 to 25 easing near noon.

My pick is Porteau now until about 11am, NNE 20 to 22 with waves. The tide topped out at 15.1ft at 7:16am and ebbs all morning. Check before driving: Pam Rocks 22 or more on the 8am reading, go; under 20, stay home.

2026-11-08.text:
Howe Sound is way ahead of the page this morning. At 6:53am the Spit was SSE 28 gusting 37 (page about 16), and Pam Rocks read SSE 25 at 6am. Pemberton sits 5 hPa below Vancouver, so the inflow should keep pulling.

My pick is Squamish from first light (about 7:45am) into early afternoon, SSE 25 to 29 with gusts near 38. Small kites, experienced riders only. Check before driving: if the Spit still reads 20 or more at 9am, go.

Porteau is the backup until about 11:30, before the flood kills the swell. The Strait is softer than shown, Sand Heads only S 16.

2026-11-07.text:
Outflow day in Howe Sound. Environment Canada has a gale warning, northerly 25 to 35 this morning. At 5am Pam Rocks read only N 8 gusting 15, so it's behind the page for now, but the English Bay buoy already has NNE 15 and Pemberton is 2 hPa above Vancouver.

My pick is Porteau from 9am to 1pm, NNE 26 to 28 on the page, with swell up to about 3.5ft around midday. The tide drops to 9.8ft near 11am, then floods. Go if Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north by 9am.

Late afternoon, Howe Sound may flip to a southerly inflow.

2026-11-06.text:
Gale day in the Strait. At 5am Sand Heads reads E 20 and Halibut Bank ENE 23 gusting 28: right on size, still more east than the page's SE. Environment Canada has southeast 35 this morning, easing to 20 to 30 by noon.

My pick is Boundary Bay from noon to 5:30pm, SSE 20 to 24 gusting 30. You need 10ft of tide, so not before noon (high 13.6ft at 3:47pm). Advanced riders: Tsawwassen south side, 22 to 28 with 2ft waves. Go if Sand Heads has swung SE by 11am.

2026-11-05.text:
Inflow day in Howe Sound, but it hasn't started yet. Pam Rocks read SSE 2 at 5am, and the Squamish terminal sensor had WSW 11 gusting 14 at 5:30am. Environment Canada still has a strong wind warning for southerly inflow, but the 4am update backed off to 15 to 25 (it was 20 to 30 last night). The page has Porteau at only 5 to 9, with Pam Rocks peaking around 13 at 3pm. Pemberton is about 1 hPa below Vancouver, not the 2 to 3 that gave us the big inflow on Oct 27.

Porteau is a maybe for the afternoon, noon to 4pm. A good inflow needs about 14 from the south at Pam Rocks, so if it reads 14+ by noon, go. The tide floods from 7.8ft at 9:09am to 14.8ft at 3:29pm, which can flatten the swell. Squamish is the same call: the page has 9 to 11 from 1pm to 4pm, so watch the terminal sensor for 15+.

The Strait is light this morning, building to SE 15 to 20 near noon. Advanced riders: Tsawwassen south side, 11 to 12 from 11am.

Friday is the day: gale warning, SE 25 to 35 in the Strait Friday morning.

2026-11-04.text:
Outflow is holding. Pam Rocks reads N 18 gusting 23 at 6am, up from 16 at 5am and ahead of the page's 14. Pemberton is still 3 hPa above Vancouver, and Environment Canada's 4am update keeps northerly 15 to 25 easing near noon.

Porteau is a maybe from first light at 7:32 to about 10:30. Low tide is 6.7ft at 8:05, then it floods to 15ft by 3pm, which can flatten the swell. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go. Under 20, stay home. Squamish is an outflow, so skip it.

Thursday afternoon the southeast fills in hard, 25 to 35 in the Strait.

2026-11-03.text:
Pam Rocks woke up: N 17 at 6am, N 25 at 7am. The page now has Porteau at NNE 21 with about 3ft of swell from 8 to 10:30am, shutting off by 11.

Porteau may be the call, but the window may be short, so go now. The tide floods from 5.6ft at 6:54am toward 15.2ft at 2:21pm, which can flatten the swell. If Pam Rocks drops under 22 at 8 or 9am, turn around. On Sunday the cove had only 5 with Pam Rocks at 24, so look before you rig.

2026-11-02.text:
Quiet Monday. Pam Rocks read NNE 16 at 6am and has sat at 15 to 17 since 2am, well short of the 22 Porteau needs. Environment Canada has backed off to northerly 20 to 30, easing to 15 to 20 near noon, and the page keeps Porteau under 3, so I don't think it builds.

I'm not driving anywhere today. If Pam Rocks jumps to 22 or more from the north before 9am, Porteau is worth a look, but don't count on it. Squamish is an outflow, and showers come this afternoon.

Tuesday looks light too.

2026-11-01.text:
Outflow morning, and Pam Rocks is ahead of the page. It read NNE 25 gusting 29 at 6am after 28 to 29 overnight. Pemberton is 2.5 hPa above Vancouver and holding, and Environment Canada has a gale warning for Howe Sound: northerly 20 to 30, easing to 15 early this afternoon. The page drops Porteau to 11 by 8am, but I think it holds longer.

My pick is Porteau from first light (7:26am) to about 9:30am, NNE 20 to 25 with 3ft of swell early. Go early: the tide floods from 5.8ft at 7am to a 15.5ft high at 12:46pm, which may flatten the swell as it fills. If Pam Rocks drops under 22 it's done.

Everywhere else is light. Sand Heads has NNW 13, offshore for Boundary Bay, and Point Atkinson is E 3. Squamish is an outflow, so boat only.

2026-10-31.text:
Light morning, but the outflow is building. Pam Rocks is up to N 16 at 9am from 13 at 7am, Pemberton is now 2 hPa above Vancouver and climbing, and Environment Canada calls Howe Sound northerly 20 to 30 by early evening. The page hasn't caught it yet.

So Porteau is my late maybe, about 3:30pm to last light around 6:15pm, on the ebb down to 11.9ft at 5:34pm. Check before driving: if Pam Rocks reads 22 or more from the north by 2:30pm, go.

Backup is Tsawwassen south side, 3pm to 6pm, NW 9 to 10, advanced riders only
